Occurrences.Kwic: 教外別傳者目之為禪。此禪即一心之異名
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Tianmu Zhongfeng (天目中峰廣錄): Zhongfeng Mingben says what is termed the separate transmission is called Chan and that this Chan is another name for the one mind.

Senses.Explanation: Chan records use this phrase as a lineage charter, a recurring interview question, and an object of explicit qualification about what “outside” and “separate” do not mean. The flower case places it beside not setting up words and entrustment to Mahakasyapa. Yuanwu repeats it in the four-part banner, while Yunmen asks why it is asserted when the canon is hardly wordless. Unnamed monastics ask Gushan and Shishuang what the transmitted matter or phrase is. Zhongfeng Mingben distinguishes speech and writing from what is separately transmitted, calls the latter Chan and another name for the one mind, and elsewhere denies that it is some additional teaching outside mind. The corpus thus supplies a transmission claim, not a warrant to erase its recorded verbal uses.
